starting-off-talking-to-velorina.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo
You cannot understand the ghost.

starting-off-talking-to-velorina.text: If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

starting-off-talking-to-velorina.speaker: Velorina
starting-off-talking-to-velorina.text: Take pity on me, please - eternity stretches out before me and I am helpless in its grasp.

steps.player: Why, what is the matter?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry - I was just wailing out loud. I didn't mean to scare you.

steps.player: No, that's okay - it takes more than a ghost to scare me. What is wrong?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Do you know the history of our town?

options.text: Yes, I do. It is a very sad story.

steps.player: Yes, I do. It is a very sad story.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Would you help us obtain our release into the next world?

steps.player: No - could you tell me?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Do you know why ghosts exist?

steps.player: A ghost is a soul left in limbo, unable to pass over to the next world; they might have something left to do in this world that torments them, or they might just have died in a state of confusion.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!

steps.player: Why on earth would you do such a thing?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands of Gielinor. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands.  Then, Necrovarus came to us.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm. He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.

steps.player: That's a very sad story.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Would you help us obtain our release into the next world?

steps.player: Yes, of course I will. Tell me what you want me to do.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Oh, thank you!

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Necrovarus will not listen to those of us who are already dead. He might rethink his position if someone with a mortal soul pleaded our cause.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: If he declines, there may yet be another way.

steps.player: I'm sorry, but it isn't really my problem.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: No, you're right - it's our own fault. If you do change your mind though, please come back and help us. We will be here ... forever.

steps.player: Leave me alone - I'm scared of ghosts!!!

starting-off-talking-to-velorina-again.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: I sense that you have not yet spoken to Necrovarus.

steps.player: No, I was just getting to that.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Well, I suppose we do have all the time in the world...

talking-to-necrovarus.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo
You cannot understand the ghost.

talking-to-necrovarus.text: If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.player: I must speak with you on behalf of Velorina.

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: You dare to speak that name in this place?????

steps.player: She wants to pass-

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: Silence!! Or I will incinerate the flesh from your bones!!!

steps.player: But she-

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: Get out of my sight!! Or I promise you that you will regret your insolence for the rest of eternity!!!

talking-to-necrovarus-talking-to-necrova.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.player: Please, listen to me-

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: No - listen to me. Go from this place and do not return, or I will remove your head.

returning-to-velorina-after-talking-to-n.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.player: I'm sorry, but Necrovarus will not let you go.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: I feared as much. His spirit is a thing of fire and wrath.

steps.player: You spoke of another way.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: It is only a small chance. During the building of the Ectofuntus one of Necrovarus's disciples spoke out against him. It is such a long time ago I cannot remember her name, although I knew her as a friend.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: She fled before the Ectofuntus took control over us, but being a disciple of Necrovarus she would have been privy to many of his darkest secrets. She may know of a way to aid us without Necrovarus.

options.text: Do you know where this woman can be found?

steps.player: Do you know where this woman can be found?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: I have a vision of a small wooden shack, the land it was built on the unholy soil of Morytania. I sense the sea is very close, and that there are looms castles to the west and the east.

options.text: If it was such a long time ago, won't she be dead already?

steps.player: If it was such a long time ago, won't she be dead already?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: She was a friend of mine. Had she died, I would have felt her spirit pass over to the next world, though I may not follow.

returning-to-velorina-after-talking-to-n.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

options.text: Do you know where this woman can be found?
If it was such a long time ago, won't she be dead already?

talking-to-the-old-crone.player: Were you once a disciple of Necrovarus in the Temple of Phasmatys, old woman?

talking-to-the-old-crone.speaker: Old crone
talking-to-the-old-crone.text: I don't remember; I am so old and my memory goes back only so far...

talking-to-the-old-crone.player: Is there anything that can help to refresh your memory?

talking-to-the-old-crone.speaker: Old crone
talking-to-the-old-crone.text: Yes, I would love a nice hot cup of nettle tea.
If the player already has a bowl of nettle tea:

steps.player: Here's some tea for you, like you asked.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Yes, but it's not in my special cup! I only ever drink from my special cup!!

steps.player: I see. Can I have this special cup, then?

steps.text: The old crone gives you her special cup.
a porcelain cup, in the inventory or on the ground if no inventory space

talking-to-the-old-crone.text: If the player does not already have a bowl of nettle tea:

steps.player: Do you know where I can find nettles around here?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: I believe they grow wild in the Haunted Forest.

talking-to-the-old-crone.text: If the player has regular nettle tea:

steps.player: Here's a lovely cup of tea for you, in your own special cup.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Oh no, it hasn't got milk in it. I only drink tea with milk, I'm afraid.

talking-to-the-old-crone.text: If the player has nettle tea with milk:

steps.player: Here's a lovely cup of milky tea for you, in your own special cup.

steps.text: As the old woman drinks the cup of milky tea, enlightenment glows from within her eyes.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Ah, that's better. Now, let me see... Yes, I was once a disciple of Necrovarus.

steps.player: I have come from Velorina. She needs your help.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Velorina? That name sounds familiar...

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Yes, Velorina was once a very good friend! It has been many years since we spoke last. How is she?

steps.player: She's a ghost, I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: They are all dead, then. Even Velorina. I should have done something to stop what was happening, instead of running away.

steps.player: She and many others want to pass on into the next world, but Necrovarus will not let them. Do you know of any way to help them?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: There might be one way...

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Do you have such a thing as a ghostspeak amulet?
If the player does not have a ghostspeak amulet in their bag:

steps.player: No I don't, I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Well, you'll need to find one.
If the player has a ghostspeak amulet in their bag:

steps.player: Yes, I'm carrying one in my bag.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Well, that's a stroke of luck.
If the player is wearing the ghostspeak amulet:

steps.player: Yes, I'm wearing one right now.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Well, that's a stroke of luck.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: There is an enchantment that I can perform on such an amulet that will give it the power of command over ghosts. It will work only once, but it will enable you to command Necrovarus to let the ghosts pass on.

steps.player: What do you need to perform the enchantment?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Necrovarus had a magical robe for which he must have no more use. Only these robes hold the power needed to perform the enchantment.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: All his rituals came from a book written by an ancient sorcerer from the East called Haricanto. Bring me this strange book.

options.text: You are doing so much for me - is there anything I can do for you?

steps.player: You are doing so much for me - is there anything I can do for you?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: I have lived here on my own for many years, but not always. When I left Port Phasmatys, I took my son with me. He grew up to be a fine boy, always in love with the sea.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: He was about twelve years old when he ran away with some pirates to be a cabin boy. I never saw him again.

steps.player: That's the second saddest story I have heard today.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: If you ever see him, please give him this...and tell him that his mother still loves him.
The old woman gives you a toy boat.
a Model ship

steps.player: Was this his boat?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Yes, he made it himself. It is a model of the very ship in which he sailed away. The paint has peeled off and it has lost its flag, but I could never throw it away.

steps.player: If I find him, I will pass it on.

options.text: Remind me - what can I do about Necrovarus?

steps.player: Remind me - what can I do about Necrovarus?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Do you have such a thing as a ghostspeak amulet?
If the player doesn't have the ghostspeak amulet:
If the player is wearing or has the ghostspeak amulet in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: There is an enchantment that I can perform on such an amulet that will give it the power of command over ghosts. It will work only once, but it will enable you to command Necrovarus to let the ghosts pass on.

steps.player: What do you need to perform the enchantment?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Necrovarus had a magical robe for which he must have no more use. Only these robes hold the power needed to perform the enchantment.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: All his rituals came from a book written by an ancient sorcerer from the East called Haricanto. Bring me this strange book.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: I cannot read the strange letters of the eastern lands. I will need something to help me translate the book.

options.text: What did you want me to get for you?

steps.player: What did you want me to get for you?

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Necrovarus had a magical robe for which he must have no more use. Only these robes hold the power needed to perform the enchantment.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: All his rituals came from a book written by an ancient sorcerer from the East called Haricanto. Bring me this strange book.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: I cannot read the strange letters of the eastern lands. I will need something to help me translate the book.

options.text: I'll go and search for those items you asked for.

steps.player: I'll go and search for those items you need.

options.text: I am afraid I have not found your son yet.

steps.player: I am afraid I have not found your son yet.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: I never expected that you would find him - although if you do, please let me know.

options.text: Remind me - what can I do about Necrovarus?
What did you want me to get for you?
I'll go and search for those items you wanted.

talking-to-the-old-crone-making-the-nett.text: If the player puts the nettles in a bowl of water:

steps.text: You place the nettles into the bowl of water.
a bowl of Nettle-water

talking-to-the-old-crone-making-the-nett.text: If the player burns the nettle tea:

steps.text: an empty bowl

talking-to-the-old-crone-making-the-nett.text: If the player successfully cooks the nettle tea:

steps.text: You boil the water and make nettle tea.
52 Cooking experience

talking-to-the-old-crone-making-the-nett.text: If the player drinks the cup of nettle tea without milk:

steps.text: You drink the cup of nettle tea.

talking-to-velorina-after-talking-to-the.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

options.text: Do you know where I can find the Book of Haricanto?

steps.player: Do you know where I can find the Book of Haricanto?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Nobody knows what has happened to the Book. It was stolen when our port was raided by pirates many years ago, and never seen since.

options.text: Do you know where I can find the Robes of Necrovarus?

steps.player: Do you know where I can find the Robes of Necrovarus?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: I imagine they are still worn by his mortal body, which now lies in a coffin inside the Temple.

options.text: I need something to translate the Book of Haricanto.

steps.player: I need something to translate the Book of Haricanto.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: I don't really know. You could try asking some of the traders from the East - they might be able to help you.

book-of-haricanto-remodeling-the-toy-shi.text: If the player attempts to repair the toy ship without the necessary items:

steps.text: You need some silk to replace the flag, something to sew it to the boat, and something to cut the flag to the right size.

book-of-haricanto-remodeling-the-toy-shi.text: If the player uses a piece of silk, a needle, thread, or knife on the toy ship without having the rest of the items:
If the player uses either a piece of silk, needle/thread, or knife on the toy ship whilst having the rest of the items:

steps.text: You replace the toy boat's missing flag.

book-of-haricanto-remodeling-the-toy-shi.text: If the player uses the repaired model ship on the Old crone:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

book-of-haricanto-remodeling-the-toy-shi.text: If the player inspects the repaired toy ship:

steps.text: The top of the flag is white. The skull emblem is white. The bottom of the flag is white.

book-of-haricanto-remodeling-the-toy-shi.text: If the player uses [blue/red/yellow/orange/green/purple] dye on the toy ship:

steps.prompt: Which part of the flag do you want to dye?

steps.text: You dye the top of the flag [blue/red/yellow/orange/green/purple].
You dye the bottom of the flag [blue/red/yellow/orange/green/purple].
You dye the skull emblem [blue/red/yellow/orange/green/purple].

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player searches the already opened chests:

steps.text: You search the chest but find nothing.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player searches the second-to-the-last chest on the bottom right on the {{FloorNumber|uk=1}}:

steps.text: You are attacked by a giant lobster!
A giant lobster appears!

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player searches the guarded chest:

steps.text: You find a piece of a map inside the chest.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player searches the mast whilst the windspeed is low:

steps.text: You can see a tattered flag blowing in the wind. The [skull emblem/top half/bottom half] is coloured [red/blue/yellow/orange/green/purple].

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player searches the mast whilst the windspeed is high:

steps.text: You can see a tattered flag blowing in the wind. The wind is blowing too hard to make out any details.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player attempts to open the chests to the north-east and south-west near the mast:

steps.text: The chest is locked.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player searches the boxes near the mast:

steps.text: There is nothing interesting in these boxes.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player attempts to open the locked chest:

steps.text: The chest is locked.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player talks to the dead pirate captain:

steps.text: The pirate captain ignores you and continues to stare lifelessly at nothing, as he has clearly been dead for some time.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player uses the chest key on the chest:

steps.text: You unlock the chest.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: If the player opens the chest:

steps.text: You find a piece of a map inside the chest.
a map scrap

steps.player: What is your name?

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: I don't remember. Everyone around here just calls me 'boy'.

steps.player: You're the cabin boy?!?

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: Yes, and proud of it.

options.text: Can I have the key to the chest?

steps.player: Can I have the key to the chest?

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: Hang on, let me ask the Captain ...
The old man cocks an ear towards the Pirate Captain's skeleton.

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: The Captain says no.

steps.player: Is this your toy boat?

steps.text: The old man inspects the toy boat.
If the model ship is broken:

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: No - I made a toy boat a long while ago, but that one had a flag.
If the model ship is fixed but not recoloured/coloured wrong:

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: No - I made a toy boat a long while ago, but the colours on the flag were different.
If the model ship is fixed and correctly recoloured:

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: My word - so it is!!! I never thought I would see it again!! Where did you get it from?

steps.player: Your mother gave it to me to pass on to you.

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: My mother? She still lives?

steps.player: Yes, in a shack to the west of here.

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: After all these years ...

steps.player: Can I have the key to the chest, then?

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: Hang on, let me ask the Captain ...
The old man cocks an ear towards the skeleton of the Pirate Captain.

steps.speaker: Old man
steps.text: The Captain says yes.
The old man gives you the chest key.
a chest key

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.player: I've lost my key to the chest - do you have another one?

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.speaker: Old man
book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: What? But the chest is only just over there! How on Gielinor did you lose it in that short distance?

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.player: Sorry, I won't do it again...

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: The old man grudgingly gives you another chest key.

book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.speaker: Old man
book-of-haricanto-at-the-shipwrecked-boa.text: Wonderful, wonderful! Mother's coming to get me!

options.text: Good news! I have found your son!

steps.player: Good news! I have found your son!

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Goodness! Where is he?

steps.player: He lives on a shipwreck to the east of here. He remembers you and wishes you well.

steps.speaker: Old crone
steps.text: Oh thank you!! I will travel to see him as soon as I am able!!

options.text: Remind me - what can I do about Necrovarus?
What did you want me to get for you?
I'll go and search for those items you wanted.

steps.text: You cross the gangplank.

book-of-haricanto-searching-the-rocky-is.text: If the player successfully jumps to a rock:

steps.text: 10 Agility experience

book-of-haricanto-searching-the-rocky-is.text: If the player jumps and falls onto the next rock:

steps.text: The player loses 1-3 Hitpoints.

book-of-haricanto-searching-the-rocky-is.text: If the player opens the chest at the northern-most part of the island:

steps.text: You find a piece of a map inside the chest.
a map scrap

book-of-haricanto-assembling-the-map-scr.text: If the player attempts to combine the scrap maps whilst only having two pieces:

steps.text: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo

steps.speaker: Ghost captain
steps.text: Would you like to visit Dragontooth Island? It is a most pleasant island in the sea between Morytania and the lands of the east. It'll cost you 25 ectotokens for the return trip.
If the player has at least 25 ectotokens in their inventory:

steps.player: Okay, here's 25 ectotokens. Let's go.

steps.text: After a long boat trip you arrive at Dragontooth Island.

options.text: If I pay 500 ectotokens, can I get unlimited trips?

steps.player: If I pay 500 ectotokens, can I get unlimited trips?

steps.text: If the player has 500 ectotokens in their inventory:

steps.player: If I pay 500 ectotokens, can I get unlimited trips?

steps.speaker: Ghost captain
steps.text: Yes, that seems fair. Okay, hand them over and we can set off.
The player gives the ghost captain 500 ectotokens and sails over to Dragontooth Island.
If the player does not have 500 ectotokens in their inventory:

steps.text: Yes, I'd accept that deal. But as you don't have enough ectotokens for that, would you like to pay 25 ectotokens for a trip now?

steps.player: Not now, thanks.
Not now, thanks.

steps.text: If the player is not at Dragontooth Island:
This map is for use elsewhere.
If the player is at Dragontooth Island:

steps.prompt: Which direction do you wish to walk?
How far do you wish to walk?

steps.text: The player walks 1 pace towards the selected direction.
The player walks 2 paces towards the selected direction.
The player walks 4 paces towards the selected direction.
The player walks 10 paces towards the selected direction.

book-of-haricanto-travelling-to-dragonto.text: If the player digs at the wrong location:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

book-of-haricanto-travelling-to-dragonto.text: If the player digs at the correct location:

steps.text: You unearth the Book of Haricanto.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: It's nice to see a human face around here.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: My name Ak-Haranu. I am trader, come from many far across sea in east.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: You come from the lands of the East? Do you have anything that can help me translate a book that is scribed in your language?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ak-Haranu may help you. A translation manual I have, much good for reading Eastern language.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: How much do you want for it?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ak-Haranu not want money for this book, as is such small thing. But there may be something you could do for me. I am big admirer of Robin, Master Bowman. He staying in village inn.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: What would you like me to do?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Please get Master Bowman sign an oak longbow for me, so Ak-Haranu can show family and friends when returning home and become much admired. Then I give you book in exchange.

options.text: Okay, wait here - I'll get you your bow.

steps.player: Okay, wait here - I'll get you your bow.

options.text: Sorry, I have too much to do at the moment.

steps.player: Sorry, I have too much to do at the moment.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: If the player does not have an oak longbow in their inventory:

steps.player: Have you got an oak longbow that I can get Robin to sign for you?

steps.speaker: Ak-Haranu
steps.text: No, Ak-Haranu afraid that no longbow in supply at moment. You must make one or buy one.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: If the player has an oak longbow in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Ak-Haranu
steps.text: How Master [player name] getting on with longbow?

steps.player: I'll let you know.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: If the player does not have an oak longbow in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Hey you, why don't you have a game of Runedraw with me? If you've got 25 gold pieces I've got a bag of runes we can use.
If the player does not have 25 coins:

steps.player: I don't have enough money on me for a game of Runedraw at the moment.

steps.text: If the player has at least 25 coins:

options.text: Yes, I'll give you a game.

steps.player: Yes, I'll give you a game.

steps.text: If the player wins:
You've won the game of Runedraw!

steps.player: So are you going to pay up then? You owe me [#] gold coins!

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: How about another game? I'll pay you back with the winnings.

steps.player: What if you lose again?

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Er ... we'll deal with that when we come to it.

options.text: Yes, I'll give you a game.
No, you didn't pay up the last time you lost.

steps.player: No, you didn't pay up the last time you lost.

steps.text: If the player loses:
You've lost the game of Runedraw.

steps.player: Well done, you beat me. But you still owe me [#] gold pieces.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Err ... how about another game? We can settle up after we've finished playing.

options.text: Yes, I'll give you a game.
No, you didn't pay up the last time you lost.

steps.text: If the player wins 100 coins:

steps.player: I've had enough of you not paying up - you owe me 100 gold coins. I'm going to tell the ghosts what you're doing.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Please don't do that!!! They will suck the life from my bones!!!

steps.player: How about you signing my longbow then?

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Yes, anything!!!
Robin signs the oak longbow for you.
a Signed oak bow

steps.player: How do you play Runedraw?

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Two players take turns to draw a rune from a bag, which contains ten runes in total. Each rune has a different value: an air rune is worth one point, up to a Nature rune which is worth nine points.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: If a player draws the Death rune then the game is over, and they have lost.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: A player can choose to hold if they wish and not draw any more runes, but this runs the risk of the other player drawing more runes until they have a greater points total and win.

steps.player: No, that doesn't sound fun.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Robin
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Do you want another game of Runedraw?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: I have your signed longbow for you.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ah, can it be true? You have obtained bow from Master Bowman?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: He was more than happy to oblige (cough). Here you are.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ak-Haranu gives you a translation manual in return for the signed oak longbow.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: May honour be bestowed upon you and your family!
If the player lost the Translation manual:

steps.player: I'm sorry, I seem to have lost the translation manual you gave me.

steps.speaker: Ak-Haranu
steps.text: Ah, no worry, my friend. For the gift of longbow Ak-Haranu would give a thousand books.
Ak-Haranu gives you another translation manual.
another Translation manual (in their inventory or on the ground with no inventory space)

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: If the player has the Translation manual:

steps.player: Thank you for the translation manual, Ak-Haranu - it may save many souls before long.

steps.speaker: Ak-Haranu
steps.text: And Ak-Haranu thanks you for kind gift of longbow.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player talks to Gravingas without the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo
You cannot understand the ghost.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player talks to Gravingas with the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Will you join with me and protest against the evil desires of Necrovarus and his disciples?

options.text: After hearing Velorina's story I will be happy to help out.

steps.player: After hearing Velorina's story I will be happy to help out.

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: I'd give you a petition form, but you look like you're carrying too much already.
If the player has one free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Excellent, excellent!! Here - take this petition form, and try and get 10 signatures from the townsfolk.
a Petition form

options.text: I'm sorry, I don't really think I should get involved.

steps.player: I'm sorry, I don't really think I should get involved.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player attempts to drop the petition form:

steps.text: You drop the petition form; it blows away in the wind.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player loses the petition form:

steps.player: I'm sorry, I seem to have lost my petition form.

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Blown away in the sea breeze, hey? Oh well, can't be helped. I'd give you another one, but you look like you're carrying too much already.
If the player has one free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Blown away in the sea breeze, hey? Oh well, can't be helped. Here's another one, but you'll have to start from scratch again.
a Petition form

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player has no signatures:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Come on - you haven't even started yet! You need 10 more signatures.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player has one signature:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Well, that's a start I suppose You need [#] more signatures.

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Not doing bad I see! You need 6 more signatures.

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Are you sure you haven't done this type of thing before? You need 3 more signatures.

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: Very nearly there!! Only 1 more signature to go.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-gravingas.text: If the player has all 10 signatures:

steps.speaker: Gravingas
steps.text: You've got them all! Now go and present it to Necrovarus!!

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: Greetings, traveller. Welcome to 'The Green Ghost' Tavern. What can I do you for?

steps.player: Can I buy a beer?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Sorry, but our pumps dried up over half a century ago. We of this village do not have much of a thirst these days.

steps.player: Can I hear some gossip?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: I suppose, as long as you keep it to yourself...

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: You see Gravingas out there in the marketplace? He speaks for the silent majority of Port Phasmatys, for those of us who would prefer to pass over into the next world.

options.text: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.player: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: That's a long story, my friend, but you look like you have the time...

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Do you know why ghosts exist?

steps.player: A ghost is a soul left in limbo, unable to pass over to the next world; they might have something left to do in this world that torments them, or they might just have died in a state of confusion.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!

steps.player: Why on earth would you do such a thing?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands of Gielinor. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands. Then, Necrovarus came to us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm. He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.

options.text: Do you have any jobs I can do?

steps.text: If the player does not have a bedsheet in their inventory:

steps.player: Do you have any jobs I can do?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Yes, actually, I do. We have a very famous Master Bowman named Robin staying with us at the moment. Could you take him some clean bed linen for me?

steps.player: Yes, I'd be delighted.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Oh, thank you. Be careful with that Robin, though - he's far too full of himself, that one.
a Bedsheet

options.text: No, I didn't mean a job like that.

steps.player: No, I didn't mean a job like that.

steps.text: If the player already has a bedsheet in their inventory

steps.player: Do you have any jobs I can do?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Well, you could take that bedsheet through to Robin like I asked.

steps.player: Nothing, thanks.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player has a clean bedsheet in their inventory:

steps.player: I've brought you a clean bedsheet, Robin.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Well it's about time. Run along now, I need some Robin time.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player does not have a clean bedsheet (or has a slimy bedsheet) in their inventory:

steps.player: So, still here then?

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player uses the bedsheet on a bucket of water or milk:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player uses the bedsheet on a bucket of slime:

steps.text: You dip the bedsheet in the bucket of ectoplasm.
an ectoplasm-covered bedsheet

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player attempts to leave Port Phasmatys whilst wearing the slimy (or regular) bedsheet:

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player attempts to wear the slimy (or regular) bedsheet outside Port Phasmatys:

steps.text: I'll only wear the bedsheet inside Port Phasmatys!

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: If the player is not wearing an amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo
You cannot understand the ghost.

steps.text: If the player is not wearing a slimy bedsheet:

steps.player: Would you sign this petition form, please?

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: I'm sorry, but it's hard to believe that a mortal could be interested in helping us.
If the player is wearing a bedsheet but not slime covered:

steps.player: Would you sign this petition form, please?

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Why are you wearing that bedsheet? If you're trying to pretend to be one of us, you're not fooling anybody - you're not even green!!
If the player is wearing a slime covered bedsheet:

steps.player: Would you sign this petition form, please?

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Most certainly, I will.
The ghost signs your petition. You have obtained [#] signature[s] so far.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: I'll do anything that annoys Necrovarus.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Yes! It's about time somebody did something about Necrovarus.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Yes, of course.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: It'll cost you...

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: I will if you make it worth my while...

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: You scratch my back and I'll scratch yours...

steps.player: How much?

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Oh, it'll cost you [1-3] ecto-tokens.
If the player does not have enough ecto-tokens:

steps.player: I don't have that many on me.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: No tokens, no signature.
If the player has at least [1-3] ecto-tokens:

steps.player: Okay, if you insist.

steps.text: The ghost signs your petition. You have obtained [#] signature[s] so far.

options.text: There's no way I'm giving in to corruption.

steps.player: There's no way I'm giving in to corruption.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: I will have you know that I am a fervent supporter of Necrovarus.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: How dare you accost me in the street?

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: Get lost.

steps.speaker: Ghost villager
steps.text: I don't have time for this nonsense.

If the player succeeds in getting 10 signatures:
You have succeeded in obtaining 10 signatures on the petition form!

steps.player: Thank you for your kind support.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-necrovaru.text: If the player does not have the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player has the amulet of ghostspeak:

steps.text: If the player also has the petition form (not signed or partially signed) in their inventory:

steps.player: I must let you know, Necrovarus, that I am collecting signatures from the citizens of Port Phasmatys.

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: Oh, I do admire an activist. Do let me know when you're finished, and I'll give it my fullest consideration.
If the player has a full petition form in their inventory:

steps.player: Necrovarus, I am presenting you with a petition form that has been signed by 10 citizens of Port Phasmatys.

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: A petition you say? Continue, mortal.

steps.player: It says that the citizens of Port Phasmatys should have the right to choose whether they pass over into the next world or not, and not have this decided by the powers that be on their behalf.

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: I see.

steps.player: So you will let them pass over if they wish?

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: Oh yes.

steps.player: Really?

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: NO!!!!! Get out of my sight before I burn every ounce of flesh from your bones!!!!!
The petition form turns to ashes in your hand.
a heap of ashes
In his rage, Necrovarus drops a key on the floor.

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-necrovaru.text: If the player doesn't have the bone key:

steps.player: So, have you changed your mind yet?

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: NEVER!!!!!

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: WHICH IS A VERY LONG TIME!!!!!!

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-necrovaru.text: If the player has the bone key:

steps.player: It matters not that you ignore your citizens' wishes, Necrovarus. Wheels have been set in motion, wheels that will set them free.

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: I have almost completely lost patience with you, mortal. Another word, and every threat I have uttered will be made real for you.

robes-of-necrovarus-entering-necrovarus-.text: If the player attempts to use the door without the key (or if the player did not use the key on the door):

steps.speaker: Ghost disciple

steps.player: Err, I was just curious...

steps.speaker: Ghost disciple
steps.text: Inside that room is a coffin, inside which lie the mortal remains of our most glorious master, Necrovarus. None may enter.

robes-of-necrovarus-entering-necrovarus-.text: If the player uses the bone key on the door:

steps.text: You unlock the door.

robes-of-necrovarus-entering-necrovarus-.text: If the player uses the bone key on the door again:

steps.text: The door is already unlocked.

robes-of-necrovarus-entering-necrovarus-.text: If the player opens the tomb:

talking-to-velorina.text: If the player does not have the enchanted ghostspeak amulet:
If the player is wearing the enchanted ghostspeak amulet:

steps.text: How is it going?

steps.text: Oh, kind adventurer - you are the answer to all our prayers!

steps.text: I have almost completely lost patience with you, mortal. Another word, and every threat I have uttered will be made real for you.

commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down.text: If the player has the enchanted ghostspeak amulet:

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: You dare to face me again - you must be truly insane!!!!

steps.player: No, Necrovarus, I am not insane. With this enchanted amulet of ghostspeak I have the power to command you to do my will!

steps.prompt: What do you want to command Necrovarus to do?

options.text: Let any ghost who so wishes pass on into the next world.

steps.player: Let any ghost who so wishes pass on into the next world.

steps.text: A beam of intense green light radiates out from the amulet of ghostspeak, enveloping Necrovarus in its power. His eyes become softer, and appear to stare into nothingness.

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: I - will - let ...

Yes?

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: ... ghost who so wishes ...

steps.player: I think we're almost getting there...

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: ... pass into the next world.

steps.player: Tell me a joke.

steps.text: A beam of intense green light radiates out from the amulet of ghostspeak, enveloping Necrovarus in its power. His eyes become softer, and appear to stare into nothingness.

steps.text: Knock knock

steps.player: Who's there?

steps.text: Egbert.

steps.text: Egbert no bacon.

steps.player: Do a chicken impression.

steps.text: Cluck cluck squuuaaaakkkk cluck cluck

steps.speaker: Necrovarus
steps.text: I think I've laid an egg...

commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down-talk.player: Told you I'd defeat you, Necrovarus. My advice to you is to pass over to the next world yourself with everybody else.

commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down-talk.speaker: Necrovarus
commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down-talk.text: I should fry you for what you have done...

commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down-talk.player: Quiet, evil priest!! If you try anything I will command you again, but this time it will be to throw yourself into the Endless Void for the rest of eternity.

commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down-talk.speaker: Necrovarus
commanding-necrovarus-to-stand-down-talk.text: Please no! I will do whatever you say!!

talking-to-velorina-2.speaker: Velorina
talking-to-velorina-2.text: You don't need to tell me [player name] - I sensed the removal of Necrovarus's psychic barrier!

talking-to-velorina-2.speaker: Velorina
talking-to-velorina-2.text: Here, take this as a thank you for the service that you have given us.
Velorina gives you a vial of bright green ectoplasm.

talking-to-velorina-2.speaker: Velorina
talking-to-velorina-2.text: This is an Ectophial. If you ever want to come back to Port Phasmatys, empty this on the floor beneath your feet, and you will be instantly teleported to the temple - the source of its power.

talking-to-velorina-2.speaker: Velorina
talking-to-velorina-2.text: Remember that once the Ectophial has been used you need to refill it from the Ectofuntus.
Congratulations, you've completed a quest: Ghosts Ahoy

options.text: I thought you were going to pass over to the next world.

steps.player: I thought you were going to pass over to the next world.

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: All in good time, [player name]. We stand forever in your debt, and will certainly put in a good word for you when we pass over.

steps.player: Can I have another Ectophial?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Really? You've already got an Ectophial.

options.text: I know, but can I have another one anyway?

steps.player: I know, but can I have another one anyway?

steps.speaker: Velorina
steps.text: Of course you can, you have helped us more than we could ever have hoped.
Velorina gives you a vial.

steps.player: Have I? Okay, forget it.

post-quest-dialogue-gravingas.player: Why are you still protesting? I have commanded Necrovarus to let you and your friends do as you like! There's no need for this anymore!

post-quest-dialogue-gravingas.speaker: Gravingas
post-quest-dialogue-gravingas.text: There's always a need for a healthy interest in politics.

post-quest-dialogue-old-crone.speaker: Old crone
post-quest-dialogue-old-crone.text: So Necrovarus has let the ghosts go free.... You have achieved many wonderful things, my young friend.
